title: SailPoint Engineer Domain 7 questions (7.1, 7.2, 7.3)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: An architect is explaining what happens when a script calls the Identity Security Cloud REST API. What does the API gateway do with each request before a backend service handles it?
choices: Checks the bearer token and routes the call to the right service
Decrypts the source credentials with the virtual appliance private key
Runs the request body through the identity profile transforms first
Holds the request in a queue until the next scheduled aggregation
questions.answer: Checks the bearer token and routes the call to the right service
questions.explanation: The gateway is the single entry point: it validates the token, applies limits and forwards the call to the owning microservice. Credential decryption happens on the VA, not at the gateway.

questions.stem: A developer has received an access token from the token endpoint. Which request header must carry it on every API call?
choices: X-Client-Secret, holding the personal access token secret
Cookie, holding the Admin UI session for the same user
Authorization, with the word Bearer followed by the token
Content-Type, holding the client ID of the API client
questions.answer: Authorization, with the word Bearer followed by the token
questions.explanation: Calls are authorized with an Authorization: Bearer header. The client secret is only sent to the token endpoint, never on ordinary API calls.

questions.stem: A migration script receives HTTP 429 responses. The developer changes it to fetch a new access token from the same API client every 90 calls, but the 429 responses continue. Why?
choices: Requests are counted per client ID and API version, not per token
The tenant blocks token requests for an hour after the first 429 response
Tokens issued to a script can only call list endpoints, not update endpoints
The gateway counts requests per source, so the limit applies to every client
questions.answer: Requests are counted per client ID and API version, not per token
questions.explanation: The default gateway limit is tracked per client ID and API version over a short window, so a fresh token from the same client changes nothing. The limit is not tied to sources.

questions.stem: A bulk-update job keeps hitting the API rate limit during business hours. What is the BEST change to the job?
choices: Send the calls to the tenant UI host instead of the API gateway host
Ask for a longer expires_in value in the access token request body
Pause on each 429 and retry with backoff, spreading the calls out
Reuse the Admin UI session cookie so calls bypass the gateway limits
questions.answer: Pause on each 429 and retry with backoff, spreading the calls out
questions.explanation: Honouring 429 responses with backoff keeps the job inside the shared limits. The UI host and session cookies are not supported paths for scripted API calls.

questions.stem: A security engineer decodes an access token in a JWT viewer to confirm which user levels the token carries. Where in the token is this shown?
choices: The signature section at the end of the token
The token_type field returned beside the token
The alg value in the token header section
The authorities claim in the token payload
questions.answer: The authorities claim in the token payload
questions.explanation: The payload carries claims such as tenant, identity and authorities (for example the Admin level). The signature only proves the token was not altered.

questions.stem: A script sends its API calls to https://acme.identitynow.com and they fail, although the same token works for a colleague. What should the developer fix FIRST?
choices: Switch the token request to the authorization code grant flow
Send the calls through the API gateway host, acme.api.identitynow.com
Regenerate the client secret and request a fresh access token from it
Add the colleague's user level to the developer's identity
questions.answer: Send the calls through the API gateway host, acme.api.identitynow.com
questions.explanation: REST calls must go through the API gateway at the tenant's api.identitynow.com host; the plain identitynow.com host serves the UI. The token itself is fine because it works elsewhere.

questions.stem: A developer sends a PATCH request to update an object with a JSON Patch array and receives an unsupported media type error. Which change is MOST likely needed?
choices: Send the JSON Patch array as query parameters in the URL
Set the Content-Type header to application/json-patch+json
Change the method to POST and keep exactly the same request body
Remove the Authorization header from the PATCH request
questions.answer: Set the Content-Type header to application/json-patch+json
questions.explanation: Identity Security Cloud PATCH endpoints expect a JSON Patch document with the application/json-patch+json media type. Changing the method or dropping the token would break the call in other ways.

questions.stem: A token response includes the field expires_in with a value of about 750. What does this tell the integration developer?
choices: The client secret must be rotated after that many days
The script may send that many calls before a new token
The access token stops working after that many seconds
The refresh token can be reused that many times in total
questions.answer: The access token stops working after that many seconds
questions.explanation: expires_in is the access token lifetime in seconds (roughly 12.5 minutes here). Scripts should request a new token before it lapses rather than treat it as a call budget.

questions.stem: A company is building an internal web portal where employees sign in and the portal calls Identity Security Cloud APIs as the signed-in employee. Which OAuth grant flow fits BEST?
choices: Client credentials
Refresh token only
Authorization code
Resource owner password
questions.answer: Authorization code
questions.explanation: The authorization code flow sends the user to sign in (with SSO and MFA) and returns a code the app exchanges for a token in that user's context. Client credentials has no interactive user.

questions.stem: A nightly system-to-system job pulls identity data with no person present to sign in. Which grant flow should the job use?
choices: Authorization code
Client credentials
Refresh token
Implicit grant
questions.answer: Client credentials
questions.explanation: Client credentials trades a client ID and secret for a token without user interaction, which suits scripts and integrations. Authorization code needs a browser sign-in.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to add the refresh token grant to an API client so a portal can keep users signed in. Which other grant must that client also have?
choices: Client credentials
Authorization code
Device code
Personal access token
questions.answer: Authorization code
questions.explanation: Refresh tokens are issued alongside the authorization code flow, so the client needs both grant types. Client credentials tokens do not come with a refresh token.

questions.stem: In an authorization code flow, where does the web application first send the user's browser?
choices: To the tenant token endpoint on the api.identitynow.com host
To the Personal Access Tokens page in the user's preferences
To the API Management page under the tenant's global security settings
To the tenant authorize endpoint on the login.sailpoint.com host
questions.answer: To the tenant authorize endpoint on the login.sailpoint.com host
questions.explanation: The browser goes to https://tenant.login.sailpoint.com/oauth/authorize to sign in; the app later posts the code to the api.identitynow.com token endpoint. Mixing up the two hosts is a common error.

questions.stem: A portal's authorization code sign-in fails with a redirect error right after users authenticate. What should the engineer check FIRST?
choices: That the client has the Helpdesk user level assigned to it
That the client secret is sent in the Authorization header of each call
That the app's redirect URL matches one listed on the OAuth client
That the users have created personal access tokens first
questions.answer: That the app's redirect URL matches one listed on the OAuth client
questions.explanation: The authorization code flow only returns to redirect URLs registered on the client. User levels and PATs are unrelated to the redirect step.

questions.stem: A team proposes that its web app collect users' Identity Security Cloud usernames and passwords and post them to get tokens. Why should the engineer reject this design?
choices: It only works for Admin users and fails for every other user level
It creates a new personal access token for every user who signs in
It exposes passwords to the app and bypasses SSO and MFA
It sends traffic through the virtual appliance instead of the gateway
questions.answer: It exposes passwords to the app and bypasses SSO and MFA
questions.explanation: Collecting passwords in the app hands it the user's credentials and cannot work with SSO, MFA or pass-through sign-in; the authorization code flow avoids this. It has nothing to do with VAs or PATs.

questions.stem: An API client created on the API Management page gets 403 Forbidden on an endpoint, but the same call works with an admin's personal access token. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The client credentials token has no user context, which that endpoint needs
The client's access token expired before the endpoint was called
The endpoint only accepts tokens that were issued from the login.sailpoint.com host
The admin's user level was copied to the client and then removed
questions.answer: The client credentials token has no user context, which that endpoint needs
questions.explanation: Tokens from a plain API client carry no identity, so endpoints that need user-level rights refuse them with 403. An expired token would return 401 instead.

questions.stem: A Helpdesk user creates a personal access token and uses it in a script that tries to create a new source. What happens?
choices: The call succeeds, because every personal access token has full API scope
The call is queued until an Admin approves it in the Task Manager
The call is refused, since the token has only Helpdesk rights
The call succeeds, but the source is hidden from other administrators
questions.answer: The call is refused, since the token has only Helpdesk rights
questions.explanation: A PAT acts with the user levels of the person who generated it, so a Helpdesk token cannot create sources. Scopes can narrow a token but never add rights the user lacks.

questions.stem: A developer wants to explore the APIs in Postman using their own access. Where do they create a personal access token?
choices: Admin, then Global, then Security Settings and API Management
Admin, then Connections, then the Virtual Appliances cluster page
Preferences, then Personal Access Tokens, under their own user menu
Admin, then Identity Management, then their own identity details
questions.answer: Preferences, then Personal Access Tokens, under their own user menu
questions.explanation: Any user can create a PAT from Preferences > Personal Access Tokens. The API Management page is where admins create standalone OAuth clients.

questions.stem: An engineer created a personal access token yesterday but did not save the secret and now needs it for a script. What should the engineer do?
choices: Open the token in the list and select the option to reveal its secret again
Ask SailPoint Support to read the secret back from the tenant
Use the client ID alone, since the secret is optional for PATs
Create a new token, store its secret securely, and delete the old token
questions.answer: Create a new token, store its secret securely, and delete the old token
questions.explanation: The secret is shown only once, when the token is created. The fix is a new token and removal of the unused one; the client ID alone cannot get an access token.

questions.stem: Which grant flow does a script use to turn a personal access token's client ID and secret into an access token?
choices: Authorization code
Client credentials
Refresh token
Device authorization
questions.answer: Client credentials
questions.explanation: PATs are implicitly given the client credentials grant, so the script posts the ID and secret to the token endpoint. No browser sign-in or refresh token is involved.

questions.stem: An administrator finds the New Token button disabled on the Personal Access Tokens page. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The tenant has turned off API access for every non-Admin user level
The user's identity is in a lifecycle state that blocks new tokens
The tenant's virtual appliance cluster is reporting an unhealthy status
The user hit the per-user token limit and must delete unused ones
questions.answer: The user hit the per-user token limit and must delete unused ones
questions.explanation: Each user can hold a limited number of PATs (ten), and the button is disabled at the limit. Deleting tokens that are no longer used frees a slot.

questions.stem: A long-running integration uses the personal access token of an administrator who is about to leave the company. What is the BEST design going forward?
choices: Copy the departing admin's token secret into a shared team password vault
Keep the token, since personal tokens keep working after the user is removed
Issue a token under a service identity with only the needed user level
Give every engineer on the team the Admin level so anyone can recreate it
questions.answer: Issue a token under a service identity with only the needed user level
questions.explanation: A PAT stops working when its owner loses access, so long-lived integrations should run under a non-expiring service identity with least privilege. Spreading the Admin level widens risk.

questions.stem: An engineer wants a personal access token used by a reporting script to be able to read identities but not change anything. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Limit the token to the read scopes the script needs when creating it
Create the token from an Admin account so all reads are permitted
Store the token secret in the script and rotate it every week
Request the token with the authorization code grant instead
questions.answer: Limit the token to the read scopes the script needs when creating it
questions.explanation: Scopes chosen for the token narrow what it can do within the user's rights, giving least privilege. Using an Admin token widens access instead of limiting it.

questions.stem: A new integration needs a standalone OAuth client that is not tied to any person's personal token. Where does an Admin create it?
choices: Preferences, then Personal Access Tokens, on the Admin's own menu
Admin, then Connections, then Sources and the source's settings
Admin, then Workflows, then the external trigger configuration
Admin, then Global, then Security Settings and API Management
questions.answer: Admin, then Global, then Security Settings and API Management
questions.explanation: Standalone OAuth clients are created on the API Management page under Security Settings, which only the Admin level can open. PATs are tied to the user who made them.

questions.stem: An old script uses a client ID that has no dashes, and its token requests now fail. What should the engineer do?
choices: Add dashes to the existing client ID and retry the token request
Grant the legacy client the Admin user level from the identity list page
Send the request to the login.sailpoint.com host instead
Create a new OAuth 2.0 client, because legacy clients no longer work
questions.answer: Create a new OAuth 2.0 client, because legacy clients no longer work
questions.explanation: Legacy client IDs (no dashes) are not supported; OAuth 2.0 client IDs look like GUIDs. Editing the ID or changing hosts cannot revive a legacy client.

questions.stem: A token request with grant type client credentials returns an error for an API client that was set up for a sign-in portal. What is the MOST likely fix?
choices: Add the client credentials grant type to the client or create a separate client
Add the refresh token grant type so the client can renew its token
Register an extra redirect URL for the script on the existing portal client
Give the portal's signed-in users the Report Admin user level
questions.answer: Add the client credentials grant type to the client or create a separate client
questions.explanation: A client only supports the grant types listed on it, so a portal client with only the authorization code grant cannot do client credentials. Redirect URLs apply to the code flow only.

questions.stem: A reporting integration only reads identities and accounts. How should the engineer set up its API client to follow least privilege?
choices: Give the client only the read scopes its endpoints need
Give the client the all-scopes value so no call is refused
Share one client between every integration in the company
Give the client every grant type so it can fall back if one fails
questions.answer: Give the client only the read scopes its endpoints need
questions.explanation: Narrow scopes limit the damage if the secret leaks. The all-scopes value and shared clients make one stolen secret far more dangerous.

questions.stem: A Report Admin creates a personal access token with the all-scopes value and tries to change a source through the API. What is the result?
choices: The call is refused, since scopes cannot add rights the user lacks
The call succeeds, because the all-scopes value overrides user levels
The call succeeds only if it is sent from inside the corporate network
The call creates an approval item for the source owner to accept
questions.answer: The call is refused, since scopes cannot add rights the user lacks
questions.explanation: A PAT's effective access is limited by both its scopes and its owner's user levels. A Report Admin cannot manage sources, whatever scopes the token lists.

questions.stem: A developer accidentally commits an API client's secret to a public code repository. What should the team do FIRST?
choices: Delete the commit history and keep using the same client secret
Shorten the access token lifetime on the token request
Remove the client's scopes and add them back after a day
Revoke the exposed client and issue new credentials to the integration
questions.answer: Revoke the exposed client and issue new credentials to the integration
questions.explanation: A leaked secret must be treated as compromised, so the client is removed and replaced. Rewriting history does not undo copies already taken.

questions.stem: A long-running export script fails with 401 Unauthorized about 13 minutes after it starts, every time. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The API client lacks the scope for the endpoint being called
The access token expired and the script never requested a new one
The gateway rate limit was reached for the client and version
The identity behind the token lost its Report Admin user level
questions.answer: The access token expired and the script never requested a new one
questions.explanation: Access tokens last about 12.5 minutes, so a script must fetch a new token before expires_in passes. A missing scope or user level would give 403, and rate limits give 429.

questions.stem: Service desk analysts need to invite users to register and help them reset passwords, and nothing more. Which user level should they get?
choices: Report Admin
Helpdesk
Source Admin
Cert Admin
questions.answer: Helpdesk
questions.explanation: The Helpdesk level covers inviting users, password help and viewing identity data. Source Admin would let them change source configuration they do not need.

questions.stem: An internal auditor must run searches, download reports and view task and aggregation activity on the Admin Dashboard, without changing any configuration. Which user level fits BEST?
choices: Report Admin
Admin
Role Admin
Helpdesk
questions.answer: Report Admin
questions.explanation: Report Admin gives search, reports and dashboard visibility without configuration rights. Admin would grant far more than an auditor needs.

questions.stem: A compliance analyst will design, launch and manage certification campaigns. Which user level should the engineer request for the analyst?
choices: Cert Admin
Report Admin
Source Admin
Role Admin
questions.answer: Cert Admin
questions.explanation: Cert Admin can perform every action in Certifications. Report Admin can view and download reports but cannot run campaigns.

questions.stem: An application team must configure sources, aggregate and correlate accounts, and build access profiles for all of the company's sources. Which user level is the BEST fit?
choices: Role Admin
Source Admin
Helpdesk
Cert Admin
questions.answer: Source Admin
questions.explanation: Source Admin covers sources, accounts and access profiles. Role Admin manages roles but not source configuration.

questions.stem: A regional team should manage only the sources and access profiles linked to its governance group, not the rest of the tenant. Which user level should it get?
choices: Source Admin
Helpdesk
Report Admin
Source Sub-Admin
questions.answer: Source Sub-Admin
questions.explanation: Source Sub-Admin limits source and access profile rights to the sources associated with the user's governance groups. Source Admin would cover every source.

questions.stem: A business analyst will create and maintain roles with membership criteria across the tenant. Which user level should be granted?
choices: Source Sub-Admin
Role Admin
Cert Admin
Helpdesk
questions.answer: Role Admin
questions.explanation: Role Admin creates, manages and edits roles across the tenant. Cert Admin reviews access in campaigns but does not build roles.

questions.stem: An engineer with the Source Admin level cannot see the Workflows or Event Triggers pages. Which user level does the engineer need for this work?
choices: Role Admin
Report Admin
Cert Admin
Admin
questions.answer: Admin
questions.explanation: Workflows, event triggers, identity profiles and virtual appliances are Admin-only areas. None of the other built-in levels opens them.

questions.stem: An administrator tries to give one user both Source Admin and Source Sub-Admin and the change is rejected. Why?
choices: Those two user levels cannot be assigned to the same user
Source Sub-Admin requires the user to also hold Role Admin
A user can hold only one user level at any given time
Source Admin must be approved by a governance group first
questions.answer: Those two user levels cannot be assigned to the same user
questions.explanation: Some combinations, such as Source Admin with Source Sub-Admin, are blocked. Users can otherwise hold several levels with combined rights, so a one-level limit is wrong.

questions.stem: An engineer is documenting how personal access tokens behave. Which TWO statements are correct?
choices: The token acts with the rights of the user who created it
The token's ID and secret are exchanged with the client credentials grant
Only users with the Admin level can create a personal access token
The secret can be viewed again later from the token list
The token response always includes a refresh token
answers: The token acts with the rights of the user who created it
The token's ID and secret are exchanged with the client credentials grant
questions.explanation: A PAT carries its creator's user levels and uses the client credentials grant. Any user can create one, the secret is shown only once, and refresh tokens belong to the authorization code flow.

questions.stem: Match each authentication method to how it works.

pairs.match: A script trades a client ID and secret for a token with no sign-in
The user signs in and the app exchanges a one-time code for a token
The app swaps a stored token for a new access token without a new sign-in
A user-generated ID and secret that acts with that user's rights

targets_extra: The app collects the user's password and posts it to the token endpoint
questions.explanation: Each method differs in whether a person signs in and whose rights the token carries. Collecting passwords in the app is the discouraged password pattern, not one of these methods.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order for a script that calls the API with a personal access token.
items: Generate the token under Preferences and Personal Access Tokens
Store the client ID and secret in a secure vault
Post the ID and secret to the oauth/token endpoint with the client credentials grant
Read the JWT access token from the response
Call the endpoint through the API gateway with an Authorization Bearer header
questions.explanation: The token is created and stored first, then exchanged at the token endpoint for a JWT, which the script sends on each gateway call until it expires.

questions.stem: In the identity search model, identity attributes sit under an attributes object. An analyst needs every identity whose department is Finance. Which query is correct?
choices: attributes.department:Finance
department.attributes:Finance
@department(Finance)
identity.department=Finance
questions.answer: attributes.department:Finance
questions.explanation: Identity attributes are searched by their path, attributes.department, with a colon between field and value. The @ syntax is for nested collections such as accounts and access.

questions.stem: An engineer needs identities that have a disabled account on the Active Directory source. Accounts are a nested collection on each identity. Which query is BEST?
choices: @access(source.name:"Active Directory" AND disabled:true)
@accounts(source.name:"Active Directory" AND disabled:true)
accounts.source:"Active Directory" disabled
source.name:"Active Directory" AND disabled:true
questions.answer: @accounts(source.name:"Active Directory" AND disabled:true)
questions.explanation: Conditions on one account belong inside a single @accounts() clause so they must match the same account. @access searches access items, not accounts.

questions.stem: A reviewer wants identities that hold the entitlement named VPN Users. Which search criteria fits the identity model?
choices: @accounts(type:ENTITLEMENT AND name:"VPN Users")
attributes.entitlement:"VPN Users"
entitlements:VPN AND Users
@access(type:ENTITLEMENT AND name:"VPN Users")
questions.answer: @access(type:ENTITLEMENT AND name:"VPN Users")
questions.explanation: Roles, access profiles and entitlements an identity holds are in the nested access collection, filtered by type and name. Entitlements are not identity attributes.

questions.stem: Data quality checks require a list of identities that have no value in the department attribute. Which query returns them?
choices: attributes.department:null
NOT _exists_:attributes.department
attributes.department:""
_missing_ attributes.department
questions.answer: NOT _exists_:attributes.department
questions.explanation: The _exists_ operator tests whether a field has a value, and NOT reverses it. Searching for the word null or an empty string does not find absent fields.

questions.stem: Security wants leavers who still have an enabled Active Directory account. Which query BEST matches the identity search model?
choices: attributes.cloudLifecycleState:terminated OR @accounts(source.name:"Active Directory" AND disabled:false)
@accounts(cloudLifecycleState:terminated AND source.name:"Active Directory")
@access(attributes.cloudLifecycleState:terminated AND disabled:false)
attributes.cloudLifecycleState:terminated AND @accounts(source.name:"Active Directory" AND disabled:false)
questions.answer: attributes.cloudLifecycleState:terminated AND @accounts(source.name:"Active Directory" AND disabled:false)
questions.explanation: The lifecycle state is an identity attribute and the enabled AD account is a nested account condition, joined with AND. OR would also return every active user with an AD account.

questions.stem: An onboarding report must show identities created during the last seven days. Which query should the engineer save?
choices: created:last 7 days
created>now-7d
created:[now-7d TO now]
@created(now-7d)
questions.answer: created:[now-7d TO now]
questions.explanation: Date ranges use square-bracket range syntax with date math such as now-7d. The other forms are not valid search syntax.

questions.stem: A query returns identities whose Workday account is enabled but whose disabled account is on a different source. The query is @accounts(source.name:Workday) AND @accounts(disabled:true). What is the cause?
choices: Workday accounts are stored in the access collection rather than in accounts
Separate @accounts clauses can each match a different account
The disabled field only exists on accounts from directory-type sources
The search index ignores Boolean operators placed between nested clauses
questions.answer: Separate @accounts clauses can each match a different account
questions.explanation: Each @accounts() clause is evaluated on its own, so different accounts can satisfy each one. Putting both conditions inside one clause forces them onto the same account.

questions.stem: The query attributes.department:Sales and attributes.location:Austin returns far more identities than expected. What is the MOST likely problem?
choices: Location values must always be wrapped in square brackets
Two identity attributes cannot be combined in one query
The department field must always be searched with the @access syntax
The Boolean operator is lowercase, so it is not treated as AND
questions.answer: The Boolean operator is lowercase, so it is not treated as AND
questions.explanation: Search operators AND, OR and NOT must be written in capitals; lowercase and is treated as a term. Combining attributes is normal.

questions.stem: An analyst searches for accounts on a source named Active Directory with source.name:Active Directory and gets wrong results. How should the value be written?
choices: Join the words with a plus sign and drop the field name
Replace the space with an underscore in the source name
Wrap the value in double quotes so it is one phrase
Put the value inside an @source clause with no field name
questions.answer: Wrap the value in double quotes so it is one phrase
questions.explanation: A value with spaces must be quoted, such as source.name:"Active Directory", or the second word is searched separately. Underscores change the value itself.

questions.stem: An engineer needs identities whose name starts with adm, such as admin01 and admjones. Which query works?
choices: name:adm%
name:like adm
name:[adm]
name:adm*
questions.answer: name:adm*
questions.explanation: The asterisk is the wildcard for any number of characters. The percent sign and like are SQL habits that the search syntax does not use.

questions.stem: A risk review needs identities with more than 50 access items. Which query is correct?
choices: accessCount:>50
accessCount:over 50
@access(count>50)
accessCount=50+
questions.answer: accessCount:>50
questions.explanation: Numeric fields accept comparison operators after the colon, as in accessCount:>50. The other forms are not supported.

questions.stem: A free-text search for Smith returns identities named Smith and also identities whose manager is named Smith. What should the analyst do to return only people with that last name?
choices: Search a named field, for example attributes.lastname:Smith
Add a wildcard to the end, for example Smith*
Write the term in lowercase, for example smith
Wrap the term in parentheses so it is searched exactly, for example (Smith)
questions.answer: Search a named field, for example attributes.lastname:Smith
questions.explanation: An unqualified term matches across many fields, including related manager data. Naming the field limits the match; a wildcard would widen it.

questions.stem: An analyst needs identities in either the Sales or the Marketing department who are not managers. Which query is BEST?
choices: (attributes.department:Sales OR attributes.department:Marketing) AND NOT isManager:true
attributes.department:Sales OR attributes.department:Marketing NOT isManager:true
attributes.department:(Sales AND Marketing) AND isManager:false
attributes.department:Sales,Marketing NOT isManager
questions.answer: (attributes.department:Sales OR attributes.department:Marketing) AND NOT isManager:true
questions.explanation: Parentheses group the OR so the AND NOT applies to both departments. Using AND between the departments would require one identity to be in both.

questions.stem: A company wants Identity Security Cloud notifications to come from noreply@acme.com instead of the default sender. What must happen before the address can be selected as the live From address?
choices: The address must be added as an identity attribute on every profile
A virtual appliance must be configured as the outbound mail relay
Each email template must be edited to hard-code the new sender
The address or its domain must first be verified
questions.answer: The address or its domain must first be verified
questions.explanation: Addresses must be verified (by the emailed link or a verified domain) before use as the From address, set under System Settings > Product Branding. Mail is sent by the cloud, not relayed through a VA.

questions.stem: The mail team says its email security checks DKIM signatures. What must the engineer do so notifications from a custom From address pass?
choices: Publish an SPF record listing the virtual appliance IP addresses
Upload the company's mail server certificate to the tenant
Ask users to add the sender address to their safe senders list
Add the domain and publish the CNAME records it provides in DNS
questions.answer: Add the domain and publish the CNAME records it provides in DNS
questions.explanation: DKIM domain verification works by publishing the provided CNAME records, after which the domain shows as verified. SPF is handled by the sending service, and VAs do not send notification mail.

questions.stem: An organization authenticates email with SPF only, with no DMARC policy. Which extra configuration does Identity Security Cloud need for its notifications?
choices: A custom MAIL FROM domain published with TXT and MX records
A DKIM CNAME record published for every user's mailbox
None, because SPF is handled by the sending email service
A virtual appliance in the mail network to relay the messages
questions.answer: None, because SPF is handled by the sending email service
questions.explanation: SailPoint sends through Amazon SES, which takes care of SPF for plain SPF checks. A custom MAIL FROM domain is needed when DMARC must be satisfied through SPF.

questions.stem: An organization enforces DMARC and satisfies it through SPF alignment. What should the engineer configure?
choices: A second From address on a public webmail domain for backup
A custom MAIL FROM domain that is a subdomain of the From address domain
A MAIL FROM domain that is also in use as a user mailbox domain for staff
The default sender, since DMARC never applies to cloud mail
questions.answer: A custom MAIL FROM domain that is a subdomain of the From address domain
questions.explanation: To align SPF for DMARC, a custom MAIL FROM subdomain (not used to send or receive mail) is published with the TXT and MX records shown. Reusing a live mailbox domain is not allowed.

questions.stem: The team wants to use the same From address in its sandbox and production tenants, but the sandbox will not accept it. What is the BEST recommendation?
choices: Delete the address from production and add it again on the sandbox
Point the sandbox at production's virtual appliance so mail is shared
Use a separate address, for example on a sandbox subdomain
Leave the sandbox on the default sender and disable all its templates
questions.answer: Use a separate address, for example on a sandbox subdomain
questions.explanation: Each From address can be used by only one tenant unless Support intervenes, and subdomains can be verified separately per environment. A VA has nothing to do with email sending.

questions.stem: A tenant has two configured brands, one for employees and one for contractors. How can each group receive email from a different From address?
choices: Set a verified From address on each brand
Create a separate email template set for each identity profile
Add a transform that rewrites the sender on contractor identities
Configure a second tenant for contractors and send from there
questions.answer: Set a verified From address on each brand
questions.explanation: When brands are configured, the From address can be set per brand and recipients get the address of their brand. Transforms and identity profiles do not control the sender.

questions.stem: A new sandbox tenant holds copies of real employee identities. What should the engineer configure before testing lifecycle changes?
choices: Delete every email template so no messages can be sent
Change all identity email attributes to the engineer's own mailbox address
Redirect all email to a test address in the email template settings
Turn off the virtual appliance so outbound mail stops
questions.answer: Redirect all email to a test address in the email template settings
questions.explanation: Setting email to go to a test address keeps real users from receiving test notifications. Editing identity data or deleting templates is invasive and harder to undo.

questions.stem: After go-live, managers report they receive no access approval emails at all, while one engineer gets all of them. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Email settings are still set to the test address instead of intended recipients
The approval scheme was changed to use governance groups instead of managers
The managers' identities lack the Helpdesk user level
The From address domain has not yet passed DKIM checks
questions.answer: Email settings are still set to the test address instead of intended recipients
questions.explanation: While the test address is selected, every notification goes to it until the setting returns to intended recipients. A DKIM problem would affect all recipients, not route mail to one person.

questions.stem: An engineer edited an email template and wants to see the result before anyone else gets it. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Save it, set a test address and use the template's test email option
Publish the template and ask a manager to forward any message received
Trigger a real access request for a production user to generate one
Export the template and open the file in a web browser
questions.answer: Save it, set a test address and use the template's test email option
questions.explanation: Each saved template can send a test email to the test address, which shows the rendered message safely. Using real requests affects real users.

questions.stem: Managers should get an email when their reports move into the inactive lifecycle state. Where is this BEST configured?
choices: In the account aggregation schedule settings of the authoritative source
In the email settings of that lifecycle state on the identity profile
In the API Management page under the tenant security settings
In the From address settings under product branding
questions.answer: In the email settings of that lifecycle state on the identity profile
questions.explanation: Lifecycle states can send email notifications to chosen recipients when an identity enters them. The other areas do not send state-based notices.

questions.stem: A template must show the requester's display name in the message body. How should the engineer add it?
choices: Hard-code a sample name and edit it for each request
Insert the template's supported Velocity variable for the requester
Add a transform to the identity profile that writes the whole message body
Create a search subscription that appends the name
questions.answer: Insert the template's supported Velocity variable for the requester
questions.explanation: Email templates use Velocity variables that are filled in when each message is sent. Hard-coding or transforms cannot produce per-message values.

questions.stem: Auditors ask who changed the email test address last month. Where should the engineer look?
choices: Read the virtual appliance logs from the cluster page
Search the audit events, since the change is recorded as an event
Open the email template history in the From address list of the branding page
Check the identity profile's preview for the auditor
questions.answer: Search the audit events, since the change is recorded as an event
questions.explanation: A change to the test address is recorded as an audit event that can be found in Search. VAs do not handle email settings.

questions.stem: Operations wants an alert in its monitoring tool whenever a virtual appliance cluster changes health status. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Schedule a daily search subscription on identity records
Ask a Helpdesk user to check the cluster page every morning by hand
Subscribe the tool to the VA cluster status change trigger
Run a certification campaign on the VA service accounts
questions.answer: Subscribe the tool to the VA cluster status change trigger
questions.explanation: The VA cluster status change trigger pushes the event to a subscribed endpoint as it happens. Manual checks and daily searches miss outages between runs.

questions.stem: The identity team must know when an account aggregation from its HR source fails, without watching the console. What should the engineer set up?
choices: An aggregation completed trigger or workflow that alerts on failure
A search subscription for identities created in the last day by that source
A lifecycle state that disables accounts after aggregation
A role whose membership criteria check aggregation results
questions.answer: An aggregation completed trigger or workflow that alerts on failure
questions.explanation: The account aggregation completed event reports the status of each run, so a subscription or workflow can alert on errors. Searches for new identities would not reveal a failed run.

questions.stem: Security wants a daily email listing terminated identities that still have enabled accounts. What is the BEST way to deliver it?
choices: Save the search and create a daily subscription to it
Export the search to a file by hand at the end of each day
Create an access profile named for terminated identities
Add the query to the identity profile's attribute mappings
questions.answer: Save the search and create a daily subscription to it
questions.explanation: Saved searches can be subscribed to on a schedule so results arrive by email. Manual exports are easy to forget.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to see whether last night's aggregations and identity refresh tasks finished. Where should the engineer look FIRST?
choices: The Personal Access Tokens page in the engineer's preferences
The email template settings for the tenant
The Admin Dashboard aggregation activity and tasks views
The access request history of the engineer's identity
questions.answer: The Admin Dashboard aggregation activity and tasks views
questions.explanation: The Admin Dashboard shows aggregation activity and task status. The other pages do not report job results.

questions.stem: Monitoring alerts are currently sent to one administrator's personal mailbox. What is the BEST improvement?
choices: Send alerts to the From address used for notifications
Send alerts to a shared team mailbox or ticket queue
Turn alerts off and rely on users to report problems
Forward alerts to every identity in the tenant
questions.answer: Send alerts to a shared team mailbox or ticket queue
questions.explanation: Shared destinations keep alerts visible when one person is away or leaves. Sending to everyone or no one defeats the purpose.

questions.stem: Users report that the tenant is slow for everyone, and the team suspects a SailPoint-side incident rather than a local fault. What should the engineer check FIRST?
choices: The virtual appliance logs for the source with the most accounts
SailPoint's service status page for current platform incidents
The email template settings for redirected messages
The identity profile preview for a sample identity
questions.answer: SailPoint's service status page for current platform incidents
questions.explanation: A tenant-wide slowdown that affects every user points to the service itself, which SailPoint reports on its status page. VA logs only show connector activity on premises.

questions.stem: A source's configuration was changed yesterday and nobody admits to it. Where should the engineer look to see who made the change?
choices: Read the source's account aggregation history
Open the source's correlation configuration
Search the audit events for the source change
Check the workflow execution history
questions.answer: Search the audit events for the source change
questions.explanation: Admin configuration changes are recorded as events that can be searched by actor and target. Aggregation history only shows import runs.

questions.stem: A user's access request was approved but the Active Directory account was never created. Where is the BEST place to find the failure reason?
choices: The certification campaign report for the user's manager and department
The From address settings in the tenant branding
The role membership preview for the user's department
The account activity for that request, with each item's result
questions.answer: The account activity for that request, with each item's result
questions.explanation: Account activities track each provisioning operation and its outcome, including connector errors. Certification reports do not show provisioning results.

questions.stem: An aggregation finished but fewer accounts appear than expected. Where should the engineer look FIRST for the run's counts and errors?
choices: The Personal Access Tokens page of the source owner
The search subscription settings for the source
The aggregation activity for that source run
The email notification settings of the lifecycle state
questions.answer: The aggregation activity for that source run
questions.explanation: Aggregation activity shows how many accounts were scanned, added, changed or removed and any errors. Token and email settings are unrelated.

questions.stem: Aggregation activity shows a connector error on an on-premises JDBC source, but the message is too short to explain it. Where is the detailed connector output?
choices: The tenant's Admin Dashboard overview page
The identity details page of the source owner
The audit events recorded for the source's last configuration change
The connector log on the virtual appliance that ran the job
questions.answer: The connector log on the virtual appliance that ran the job
questions.explanation: Connector work for VA-based sources runs on the VA, whose connector log (ccg) holds the full error. The cloud views show a summary only.

questions.stem: A workflow that should have emailed a manager did nothing yesterday. Where should the engineer look to see what each step received and returned?
choices: The aggregation activity for the HR source
The email template list for the tenant
The API Management client list
The workflow's execution history
questions.answer: The workflow's execution history
questions.explanation: Execution history records each run with every step's input and output, which shows where it stopped. Email templates show content, not run results.

questions.stem: An auditor asks which administrator granted a user the Source Admin level last quarter. What is the BEST source of this record?
choices: The audit events for the identity's user level change
The identity profile's attribute mappings
The aggregation activity for the HR source on the dashboard
The tenant's From address settings
questions.answer: The audit events for the identity's user level change
questions.explanation: Granting user levels is an audited action recorded in events with actor and target. Identity profile mappings do not record admin actions.

questions.stem: Match each troubleshooting question to where the activity record is found.

pairs.item: Why an approved account was not created
How many accounts an import added
The full stack trace of a JDBC connector error
pairs.match: Connector log on the virtual appliance

questions.explanation: Each record type has its own home: events for admin actions, account activity for provisioning, aggregation activity for imports, VA logs for connector detail and execution history for workflows.

questions.stem: A company will send notifications from a custom address on its own domain and its email security checks DKIM. Which TWO actions are needed?
choices: Add the domain and publish its CNAME records in DNS
Add the address and select it as the live From address once verified
Configure the virtual appliance as an SMTP relay
Publish an SPF record listing the tenant's IP addresses
Set the email settings to the test address in production
answers: Add the domain and publish its CNAME records in DNS
Add the address and select it as the live From address once verified
questions.explanation: DKIM needs the domain verified with the given CNAME records, and the verified address is then chosen as the From address. SPF is handled by the sending service and VAs do not relay mail.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to switch notifications to a custom From address on a DKIM-protected domain.
items: Open the From address section in the product branding settings
Add the domain and copy the CNAME records shown
Have the DNS team publish the CNAME records
Wait for the domain to show as verified
Add the email address, which verifies through the domain
Select the address as the live From address and save
questions.explanation: The domain is added and verified through DNS first, which lets addresses on it verify at once; only a verified address can be made live.

questions.stem: A workflow saves but shows a validation error: the false path of a Compare Strings operator leads nowhere. What must the engineer add?
choices: An end step, Success or Failure, at the end of that branch
A second trigger placed at the start of the false branch of the operator
A Loop operator that repeats the comparison step
A Wait action between the trigger and the operator
questions.answer: An end step, Success or Failure, at the end of that branch
questions.explanation: Every branch must end in a Success or Failure end step or merge back into the main flow. A workflow can have only one trigger.

questions.stem: In the builder, a Send Email action cannot select the manager email returned by Get Identity, because Get Identity sits after Send Email. What should the engineer do?
choices: Add a second trigger that provides the manager email
Type the JSONPath of a later step into the email field
Place Send Email on the false branch of an operator
Move Get Identity so it runs before Send Email
questions.answer: Move Get Identity so it runs before Send Email
questions.explanation: Steps can only use data produced by earlier steps, so the lookup must run first. Later steps are not offered in the variable selector.

questions.stem: A workflow must send one email to Sales managers and a different email to everyone else. Which step creates the two paths?
choices: A Loop operator over the department values
A second trigger filtered on the Sales department
A Define Variable operator that holds the department
A Compare Strings operator on the department value
questions.answer: A Compare Strings operator on the department value
questions.explanation: Comparison operators evaluate a value and send the run down a true or false path. A loop repeats steps for each item; it does not branch.

questions.stem: A workflow receives a list of entitlements and must run the same steps for each one. Which step should the engineer use?
choices: The Compare Numbers operator
A Success end step
A trigger filter
The Loop operator
questions.answer: The Loop operator
questions.explanation: The Loop operator runs its inner steps once per item in a list. A comparison operator only branches once.

questions.stem: An engineer wants a Send Email body to include the identity ID supplied by the trigger. Which inline variable is correct?
choices: {trigger.identityId}
$trigger:identityId
{{$.trigger.identityId}}
[[trigger.identityId]]
questions.answer: {{$.trigger.identityId}}
questions.explanation: Inline variables use two pairs of braces around a JSONPath that starts with $ and the step name. The other forms are not recognised.

questions.stem: The same notification steps must run both when an identity is created and when an identity attribute changes. How should the engineer design this?
choices: Add both triggers to one workflow and connect them to the first action
Use one trigger and add the second as an action after the end step
Build two workflows, each with its own trigger
Put the second trigger on the true path of a Compare Strings step
questions.answer: Build two workflows, each with its own trigger
questions.explanation: Each workflow has exactly one trigger, so two events need two workflows (duplicating one saves effort). Triggers cannot be placed as actions or inside branches.

questions.stem: Two branches of a workflow must continue with the same Send Email step after their separate actions. What is the BEST design?
choices: Copy the Send Email step into each branch and add a second trigger to it
End both branches with Failure and start a new workflow
Connect the last step of both branches to the shared Send Email step
Replace both branches with a Loop operator
questions.answer: Connect the last step of both branches to the shared Send Email step
questions.explanation: Branches can merge by connecting both into the next step, which keeps one copy of shared logic. Ending in Failure would mark successful runs as failed.

questions.stem: A workflow uses the Identity Attributes Changed trigger but should run only when the lifecycle state changes. Which trigger filter is correct?
choices: $.identity.cloudLifecycleState == changed
@accounts(attribute:cloudLifecycleState)
$.changes[?(@.attribute == "cloudLifecycleState")]
attributes.cloudLifecycleState:*
questions.answer: $.changes[?(@.attribute == "cloudLifecycleState")]
questions.explanation: Trigger filters are JSONPath expressions over the trigger input, and this one keeps only changes to cloudLifecycleState. The other choices are search syntax or invalid.

questions.stem: A leaver workflow should start only when an identity's lifecycle state changes to terminated. Which filter fits BEST?
choices: $.changes[?(@.attribute == "cloudLifecycleState" && @.newValue == "terminated")]
$.changes[?(@.attribute == "cloudLifecycleState" || @.newValue == "terminated")]
$.changes[?(@.newValue == "cloudLifecycleState")]
$.changes[?(@.oldValue == "terminated")]
questions.answer: $.changes[?(@.attribute == "cloudLifecycleState" && @.newValue == "terminated")]
questions.explanation: Both conditions must hold, so they are joined with &&. Using || would also fire on any change to terminated in other attributes and on every lifecycle change.

questions.stem: Why should an engineer add a filter to a busy trigger such as Identity Attributes Changed?
choices: To make the workflow always run with the Admin user level
To allow the workflow to have more than one trigger
To send the trigger input to a virtual appliance
To avoid runs for events it does not need to handle
questions.answer: To avoid runs for events it does not need to handle
questions.explanation: Filters limit when a workflow starts, which avoids needless executions and quota use. They do not change permissions or the one-trigger rule.

questions.stem: A summary email must be sent every weekday at 7 a.m., regardless of events. Which trigger should the workflow use?
choices: A scheduled trigger
An external trigger
Identity Created
Account Aggregation Completed
questions.answer: A scheduled trigger
questions.explanation: Scheduled triggers start a workflow at set times. Event triggers depend on something happening, and an external trigger waits for an outside call.

questions.stem: A ticketing system must start a workflow by calling Identity Security Cloud when a ticket reaches a certain status. Which trigger fits BEST?
choices: An external trigger, called with its client credentials
A scheduled trigger that polls the ticketing system
The Identity Attributes Changed trigger with a filter
An Account Aggregation Completed trigger on the ticket source
questions.answer: An external trigger, called with its client credentials
questions.explanation: An external trigger gives an outside system a URL and OAuth client to start the workflow on demand. Polling on a schedule adds delay.

questions.stem: An engineer built a trigger filter in the Advanced JSONPath editor and now opens the Basic editor to adjust it. What happens?
choices: The Basic editor converts the JSONPath expression into matching conditions
Both editors stay active and are joined with AND
The filter is moved into a Compare Strings step
The Basic editor starts over and the Advanced filter is lost
questions.answer: The Basic editor starts over and the Advanced filter is lost
questions.explanation: Filters built in the Advanced editor must be kept there; switching to Basic means starting over. The editors are not merged.

questions.stem: A workflow should notify the source owner after each import from the HR source. Which trigger should the engineer choose?
choices: Identity Created
Access Request Submitted
Scheduled
Account Aggregation Completed
questions.answer: Account Aggregation Completed
questions.explanation: Account Aggregation Completed fires after each aggregation and includes the source and status. Identity Created fires only for new identities.

questions.stem: An engineer finished building a leaver workflow. What should happen before it is enabled?
choices: Enable it in production and watch the first real leaver
Test it with sample trigger input and review each step
Export it to a file and ask SailPoint to review it
Add a second trigger so it can be tested twice
questions.answer: Test it with sample trigger input and review each step
questions.explanation: Workflows should be tested with sample input before enabling, and the results show each step. SailPoint does not review workflows.

questions.stem: A saved workflow cannot be tested and the builder lists missing required fields. What is true?
choices: The workflow must be enabled first so testing becomes available
Testing is only possible after the workflow is exported to JSON
Validation errors block testing, though the draft can be saved
The fields are filled in automatically during the first test run
questions.answer: Validation errors block testing, though the draft can be saved
questions.explanation: Drafts with validation errors can be saved but not tested or enabled. Enabling does not bypass validation.

questions.stem: A workflow ran but the email it sent had a blank manager name. Where should the engineer look FIRST?
choices: The execution history, to compare each step's input and output
The From address settings in product branding
The API Management page under the tenant's global security settings
The identity profile's lifecycle state list
questions.answer: The execution history, to compare each step's input and output
questions.explanation: Execution history shows the JSON each step received and produced, which reveals where the value went missing. Branding settings only affect the sender.

questions.stem: Several workflows started failing with unauthorized errors the day their creator's account was disabled. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Re-enable the departed admin's account permanently
Raise the workflows' execution limit for the day
Assign the workflows to another active admin as owner
Remove the trigger filters from the failing workflows
questions.answer: Assign the workflows to another active admin as owner
questions.explanation: The creator becomes the owner and a personal access token is made for the workflow; when the owner leaves the token stops working. Reassigning ownership creates a new token.

questions.stem: To avoid orphaned workflows, which practice should the team adopt?
choices: Build each workflow from the personal account of the newest engineer on the team
Use an admin account that will not expire, such as a service identity
Create every workflow from a Helpdesk account with no other levels
Keep workflows disabled and run them by hand when needed
questions.answer: Use an admin account that will not expire, such as a service identity
questions.explanation: Workflow owners must be admins whose access lasts, otherwise the workflow's token becomes invalid. Helpdesk accounts cannot create workflows.

questions.stem: During a mass HR update, a per-identity workflow runs quickly in the morning but slowly late in the day. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The workflow owner's personal access token expired at noon
The daily fast-execution quota was reached, so later runs are throttled
The trigger filter switched itself to the Basic editor automatically at noon
The virtual appliance cluster paused the workflow queue
questions.answer: The daily fast-execution quota was reached, so later runs are throttled
questions.explanation: Workflows have a daily limit for the fastest executions; after it is reached, runs continue at a slower rate until the quota resets. Workflows run in the cloud, not on VAs.

questions.stem: An engineer tries to enable a new workflow and receives an error about the number of enabled workflows. What should the engineer do?
choices: Disable or remove an unused workflow, then enable the new one
Duplicate the workflow so that the copy can be enabled in its place
Change the workflow's trigger to a scheduled trigger
Remove all end steps so it counts as a draft
questions.answer: Disable or remove an unused workflow, then enable the new one
questions.explanation: The tenant caps how many workflows can be enabled at once, so another must be disabled first. A duplicate counts the same way.

questions.stem: A team has a sandbox and a production tenant. What is the BEST practice for a new transform and identity profile change?
choices: Build in production and copy the change back to the sandbox afterwards
Build in both tenants by hand at the same time
Build and test in the sandbox, then promote with Configuration Hub
Build in production during a quiet weekend window
questions.answer: Build and test in the sandbox, then promote with Configuration Hub
questions.explanation: Changes should be proven in the sandbox and moved with Configuration Hub to avoid manual drift. Building first in production puts real identities at risk.

questions.stem: Before saving a mapping change on an identity profile, how can the engineer check the new attribute values for a sample identity?
choices: Run a certification campaign for the identity
Read the VA logs after the next aggregation
Use the identity profile preview for a chosen identity
Submit a test access request on the identity's behalf and watch it
questions.answer: Use the identity profile preview for a chosen identity
questions.explanation: The preview shows calculated attribute values for one identity before the change is applied. Waiting for logs means the change is already live.

questions.stem: An engineer is planning tests for a new lifecycle transform. Which test set is BEST?
choices: One identity from the engineer's own department
Every production identity on the first full refresh
Only identities that already have the expected value in production today
Normal cases plus edge cases such as missing dates and leavers
questions.answer: Normal cases plus edge cases such as missing dates and leavers
questions.explanation: Good tests cover typical and boundary data so null or unusual values do not break the transform. Testing only easy cases hides errors.

questions.stem: After changing the correlation settings on a source, the engineer runs an aggregation but nothing seems to change for existing accounts. What should the engineer do?
choices: Run the aggregation again with optimization disabled
Delete the source and create it again from scratch
Raise the account deletion threshold on the source and aggregate again
Wait for the next scheduled certification campaign
questions.answer: Run the aggregation again with optimization disabled
questions.explanation: Optimized aggregation skips accounts that have not changed on the source, so a non-optimized run is needed to reprocess them. Deleting the source loses correlation data.

questions.stem: A new certification design is ready. What is the BEST way to test it before the quarterly campaign?
choices: Launch the full campaign and cancel it if reviewers start to complain
Send the reviewer email template to every manager
Run an aggregation with optimization disabled
Run a small campaign on a limited set of test identities first
questions.answer: Run a small campaign on a limited set of test identities first
questions.explanation: A small campaign validates scope, reviewers and emails without disturbing the business. Cancelling a live campaign leaves confusion.

questions.stem: An engineer is about to test provisioning changes in the sandbox against a test directory. Which setting helps MOST to protect real users from test noise?
choices: Grant the engineer the Helpdesk user level
Redirect all tenant email to a test address while testing
Disable optimization on every source aggregation
Remove all personal access tokens from the tenant before the test
questions.answer: Redirect all tenant email to a test address while testing
questions.explanation: Email redirection stops test notifications from reaching real people. The other changes do not affect who is notified.

questions.stem: An engineer moves a source configuration from the sandbox to production with Configuration Hub. What should the test plan include after the import?
choices: Re-creating every identity on the production tenant by hand afterwards
Re-entering and testing the source credentials in production
Deleting the sandbox tenant to avoid duplicates
Turning off all workflows in the sandbox tenant
questions.answer: Re-entering and testing the source credentials in production
questions.explanation: Secrets are not carried over in migrated configuration, so credentials must be supplied and the connection tested in the target. The sandbox is kept for future testing.

questions.stem: An API call returns 401 Unauthorized. What does this MOST likely mean?
choices: The token is valid but lacks rights for the endpoint
The token is missing, invalid or expired
The client sent too many requests in a short window
The object ID in the path does not exist
questions.answer: The token is missing, invalid or expired
questions.explanation: 401 points to a missing, malformed or expired token. A valid token without rights returns 403, too many calls return 429 and a missing object returns 404.

questions.stem: An API call returns 403 Forbidden with a freshly issued token. What should the engineer check FIRST?
choices: The user level behind the token, or whether the endpoint needs user context
Whether the token has expired since it was issued
Whether the request URL uses the correct tenant name for the gateway
Whether the request body is valid JSON
questions.answer: The user level behind the token, or whether the endpoint needs user context
questions.explanation: 403 means the token was accepted but its rights are not enough, often because the token has no user context or the user lacks the level. Expired tokens give 401.

questions.stem: A script gets 404 Not Found when fetching a source by ID, although the source is visible in the UI. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The token has expired and must be renewed
The ID in the path is wrong, such as a name instead of an ID
The client has sent too many requests
The source's VA cluster is reporting an error on its health page
questions.answer: The ID in the path is wrong, such as a name instead of an ID
questions.explanation: 404 means the resource at that path was not found, which often comes from using a name or an ID from another tenant. Token or rate problems give 401 or 429.

questions.stem: A provisioning request fails with an error that a required attribute is missing when creating the account. Where should the engineer fix this?
choices: The source's create account provisioning policy
The email template for access approvals
The API client's grant types
The workflow trigger filter
questions.answer: The source's create account provisioning policy
questions.explanation: The create profile defines which attributes are sent on account creation, so a missing required attribute is added or mapped there.

questions.stem: Every aggregation on an on-premises source fails with a connection timeout, while other sources on the same VA cluster work. What is the BEST next step?
choices: Delete the VA cluster and deploy a new one with fresh keys
Disable optimization on every other source on the cluster
Run Test Connection and read that source's VA connector log
Raise the account deletion threshold on that source
questions.answer: Run Test Connection and read that source's VA connector log
questions.explanation: A single failing source on a healthy cluster points to its own settings or network path, which the connection test and connector log reveal. Rebuilding the cluster is unnecessary.

questions.stem: A new identity attribute shows as empty for all identities after a profile change. What should the engineer check FIRST?
choices: The aggregation schedule of a non-authoritative source
The transform and mapping in the identity profile preview
The workflow execution history of an unrelated onboarding workflow
The client secret of the reporting API client
questions.answer: The transform and mapping in the identity profile preview
questions.explanation: An empty calculated attribute usually comes from a transform or mapping that returns no value, which the preview shows. Unrelated workflows or clients do not feed identity attributes.

questions.stem: A script's PATCH call to update an access profile keeps failing, while GET calls on the same object work. Which cause should the engineer check FIRST?
choices: The access token was issued by the authorization code flow instead
The body is not a JSON Patch document with the right content type
The access profile has too many entitlements to read
The tenant URL is missing the api part of the host
questions.answer: The body is not a JSON Patch document with the right content type
questions.explanation: PATCH endpoints need a JSON Patch array with the application/json-patch+json content type. A wrong host would break the GET calls too.

questions.stem: Put the steps of this new-hire workflow in the order they must run.
items: Identity Created trigger, filtered to employees
Get Identity action for the new hire's manager
Compare Strings operator on the department returned for the manager
Send Email action to the manager on the true path
Success end step
questions.explanation: The trigger starts the run, the lookup supplies the manager data, the operator branches, the action sends the message, and each branch ends in an end step.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to build and release a new workflow safely.
items: Choose the trigger and add a filter
Add the actions and operators and connect them
Add an end step to every branch and save
Test with a sample input and review the execution history
Enable the workflow
questions.explanation: The workflow is built from trigger to end steps, saved, then tested before it is enabled, so no untested logic runs on real events.

questions.stem: Match each API response to its MOST likely cause.

pairs.match: Missing, invalid or expired access token
Valid token without the needed rights or user context
Rate limit reached for the client

questions.explanation: Status codes separate token, permission, path and rate problems. A VA outage shows in aggregation or provisioning results, not as a gateway status code.

questions.stem: An engineer is writing a test plan for a new identity profile in the sandbox. Which TWO practices are BEST?
choices: Preview calculated attributes for sample identities before saving
Include identities with missing and unusual attribute values
Apply the change in production first to get real data
Let notifications go to real users so they can confirm results
Skip testing because Configuration Hub validates logic
answers: Preview calculated attributes for sample identities before saving
Include identities with missing and unusual attribute values
questions.explanation: Previewing and testing edge cases catch errors before rollout. Configuration Hub moves configuration but does not test its logic.
